evidence: the-target-is-pinned-in-hosts: rsyslog_client.pp:24-28 declares host { $target: ip => $target_ip, target => '/etc/hosts' } when target_ip is set; the fixture sets target p8lab-ubuntu2 / target_ip 192.168.56.24 (ubuntu2's hostonly_ip in nodes.yml), and the probe resolves the forward target via getent and counts exactly one /etc/hosts line for it, expecting 192.168.56.24 and 1 - what the lines produce

the-server-received-the-line-from-the-node: rsyslog_client.pp:42-55 renders forward_simple.conf.epp into 40-forward.conf (template line 20: *.* @@target:port over gtls); the effect reads the peer's received log for the node's logger token under host name puppet8node, i.e. the rendered rule actually delivered a local line to the target; the peer listener uses x509/certvalid, so delivery also proves the node presented a CA-valid certificate; probe is a no-op action, effect is read-only evidence, not the action's own output

forwarding-rule-sends-everything-over-tls: same lines 42-55 plus template lines 10,14,15,20 with check_names=false and port 6514 default render $DefaultNetstreamDriver gtls, $ActionSendStreamDriverMode 1, $ActionSendStreamDriverAuthMode x509/certvalid and *.* @@target:6514 (no PermittedPeer, no failover block, no auth-log ruleset); the probe greps exactly those lines and rsyslogd -N1 validity; expectation matches the template under the fixture (the CA/cert/key file lines named in 'what' are not grepped, but the end-to-end certvalid delivery covers them)

mismatch tls-material-is-the-nodes-puppet-identity: varies only the -CAfile given to openssl verify (system bundle instead of the Puppet CA, rsyslog_base.pp:49-71 source); the system bundle did not sign the lab certificate, so the verdict must change from OK, and the cmp/stat lines are unchanged - a real mismatch, not a broken command

mutating checks: the-peer-runs-a-tls-log-server runs only on the peer, mutates declares the package install, TLS copy under /etc/rsyslog.d/p8test-tls, server conf and restart (all the action does), effect is a read-only ss listener count; a-local-log-line-leaves-over-tls declares the node rsyslog restart + logger line, effect is ss established sessions to :6514 by rsyslogd; node probes name no other host, peer probes name no other host

purpose covered: Purpose matches the class header (rsyslog_client.pp:1 'forward its local logs to a remote rsyslog server over TLS') and code (rsyslog_base TLS material from the Puppet ssldir, optional /etc/hosts pin, *.* @@target over gtls). Together the checks test the job end to end: the rule renders and validates, the TLS files are the node's Puppet CA/cert/key and verify, the target is pinned, a logged line leaves over an established TLS session and arrives on a real x509/certvalid TLS server on the peer under the node's name. Left out and listed under uncovered: the failover target (needs a dead-target fixture variant with the peer as failover) and forward_auth_log (off by default, the imfile auth.log ruleset); the note honestly says the fixture sets neither; strictly forward_auth_log is lifted by a fixture variant rather than a new node kind, and it is an optional add-on, not the stated purpose (*.* already forwards the auth facility). check_names=true (x509/name) is likewise an untested non-default variant.
